analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing (Nov 11, 2026)
key_insights: SPX closed +1.3%, NDX +2.3%, RTY +0.9% on Nov 11, off intraday highs. The AI trade rebounded on CRWV earnings, with Memory and Neoclouds the best sub-sectors, Hyperscalers sold and Mag7 trailing SPX and NDX. Semis have roundtripped their post-election selloff.

The CRWV print was a beat and raise and appeared to resolve funding concerns. The desk says it is a positive step but not an all clear for data center and AI financing. The bond market was closed for the holiday, so the rest of the week's price action is the test, especially if PPI comes in hotter than expected after yesterday's yield surge.

US MKT INTEL is Tactically Bullish. It reads the Nov 10 CPI-driven move as a reset of bond yields higher to match growth of about 3.4% in 26Q3, with the economy on track to grow above trend into 2027.

Monetization Menu: the Tech washout looks at or near complete, though another Semis decline is possible. The desk likes broad Tech and would consider US Memory and Semis through options. It favors a Tech plus Cyclicals barbell and sees more upside in European Cyclicals than US ones, given lower positioning and valuation.

James Creager (EMEA Equities): sentiment indicators were at lows after the midterms, comparable to COVID and Liberation Day. CTAs had flipped short and momentum length hit lows, leaving fuel for the rally. He sees room for a year-end rally on positioning. EMEA high-touch flow shows no dip buying of Tech and some selling into AI and Electrification strength, so the move looks systematic-driven.

Brian Heavey (TMT): there is an inflection in AI picks-and-shovels flows only 'at the margin', not a real bullish inflection. High-touch volumes are down 56% on the holiday. He expects NVDA at best to tread water absent a change in the news cycle. SMH is trying to reclaim long-term trend lines (5-year MACD trend, 50d = 497).

Brendan Henrici (Energy/Utilities): CRWV said most of its power is online or fully permitted and under construction, and it does not expect impact from Texas policy. This matches Cembalest's view that the 37 GW due in 2027 is not at risk (75% under construction), while 37.5 GW of the 96 GW expected in 2028 may face a pause and 15 GW may face conditions.

Manish Sinha (Delta-One): SMH is up 15% but AI momentum (JPAIMOPR) remains weak. A similar pattern occurred in July and August (SMH +17% on weak AI momentum). He expects volatility to stay elevated until AI momentum recovers.
Sinha: DXY is breaking above 102 and has a negative correlation with ex-AI stocks (JPUSXAI). He suggests today's price action may be an opportunity to put on a year-end hedge.

Rob O'Dwyer (Fins): the CRWV beat reinforces the risk-on AI trade and helps large-cap banks (fees) and more so alternative managers (AI financing demand). AI credit risk remains, but financing markets are open and capital formation is accelerating.

Kaitlyn Bowman (Delta-One/Thematics): Neoclouds beat Hyperscalers by 2.3σ and Behind-the-Meter power beat the market by 2.0σ. Hyperscalers lagged the market by 2.0σ, Cyclicals ex-AI lagged Cyclicals by 2.1σ and Industrials ex-AI lagged Industrials by 1.8σ. She reads the move as renewed AI FOMO, not a broad improvement, and advises using weakness in preferred non-AI trades to re-engage selectively.

Bond yields view: the JPM recession basket (JPRECES) is +14.9% since Sep 30 while SPX is -1.7%, NDX -8.8%, SOXX -22.7% and DRAM -32.7%. The desk argues a decline in AI capex is unlikely to cause a US recession because it did little to raise jobs, and the consumer (large cash balances, full employment, improving wage growth) remains the engine.

Feroli (JPM Chief US Economist): nonresidential construction, contractor and heavy and civil engineering jobs rose 165,000 over the past year, only 0.1% of total employment. Any policy-driven pullback in data center spending should have limited impact on job growth. Professional, scientific and technical services jobs jumped 33,000, a sign the feared AI job loss is still far off.

Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 on $365 EPS and 21.9x, implying 8.4% upside from Friday's close. He estimates 2027 EPS growth of about 20%, while JPM Economics expects GDP growth to slow but stay trend-like with modest disinflation.

Dubravko's view of the unwind: it was a de-leveraging event in AI and AI-adjacent names. October was the largest single-month unwind for Long Momentum (about -11%, roughly 6 standard deviations), and Momentum L/S fell about 40% from its peak. Equity multiples compressed about 4x since January. AI multiples fell about 35% since May (Semis 52%, hyperscalers 14%, Memory 60%, Processing Units 50%).

Dubravko sees the selling as far along: Momentum crowding reset from 100th to 76th percentile, levered ETF sales of about $60bn Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday, CTAs net short with about $50bn left to sell, dealer net gamma imbalance at the 12th percentile, $1.2T of announced buybacks, and QQQ RSI below 30 (on average about +4% over the next five trading days).

Dubravko's catalysts: Middle East developments, MegaCap IPOs, next month's ERCOT meeting (AI capex implications) and the December Fed meeting. He sees the midterms as a clearing event and data center headwinds as less onerous than priced.

Dubravko's AI capex sensitivity: every $100B of additional capex adds about $9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS (about 2.5% growth). Capex of about $1.5T in 2027 implies about $18 of EPS versus consensus, adding 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth. JPM credit analysts expect hyperscalers to fund 2027 capex absent credit shocks, but the funding mix needs more equity.

Europe: SXXP set a new all-time high. Energy and TM led, Momentum and Beta led Value and Size, and Cyclicals beat Defensives. ECBspeak skews hawkish with a December hike fully priced. The Bundesbank sees German growth revised higher next month.

News links include Goolsbee calling the inflation report 'borderline disturbing' as the Fed weighs more hikes, a Reuters piece on a possible 50 bps hike under Warsh's Fed, and CRWV CEO Intrator cancelling a planned share sale program.

market_movers.rationale: Beat-and-raise earnings that appeared to ease funding concerns triggered an AI trade rebound. The desk cites +20% (Creager), +15% pre-market (O'Dwyer), and its CEO cancelling a planned share sale.
Heavey expects the stock to tread water at best absent a change in the news cycle. He sees only a marginal, not real, inflection in AI picks-and-shovels flows.

sector_views.rationale: The Tech washout appears at or near complete. The desk likes broad Tech, would consider Memory and Semis through options, and notes the risk of another Semis decline.
The desk sees more upside than in US Cyclicals because of lower positioning and valuation.
Less near-term upside but attractive medium-term prospects with room to re-rate (Dubravko). They lagged on the day.
Affordability is a headwind tied to oil prices, borrowing costs and housing shortages. Dubravko sees longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail versus Energy.
The trade is less compelling after moving from the 0th to the 25th percentile. Best opportunity is Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples.

earnings_insights: CRWV reported on Nov 10: beat and raise, per JPM desk commentary. No EPS or revenue figures are given in this note.
Reassuring results from IFX and ENR were also cited as helpful for sentiment, with no figures given.
Dubravko's YE26 SPX target uses $365 EPS at 21.9x. Each $100B of 2027 AI capex adds about $9 to S&P 500 EPS (his estimate, not a reported figure).
Earnings due Nov 12 (US): ALM, AMAT, BRUN, CBRS, CSCO, FIGR, FPS, FRMI, IRON, LGN, NUAI, OFRM, ONDS, SLS, TE, TWST, XE.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The desk says growth is above trend and supports the case for yields resetting higher and a Tactically Bullish stance.
Yields surged on Nov 10 after CPI. The bond market was closed on Nov 11, so a hot PPI would be the next test.
A stronger dollar has historically weighed on ex-AI stocks, and Sinha frames it as a chance to add a year-end hedge.
Oil prices are cited as a headwind for Consumer Cyclicals through affordability.
ECBspeak skews hawkish, which supports European yields and fits a view that rates are still moving higher.
Named as a catalyst by Dubravko. A Goolsbee comment in the news links says the Fed is weighing more hikes.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Feroli reads it as a sign that AI-related job loss is still far off, while cautioning against over-reading one month.

risk_factors: Another Semis decline remains possible, and AI momentum is still weak (Sinha, Monetization Menu).
A hotter than expected PPI print on Nov 13, following the yield surge after CPI.
AI and data-center credit risk remains, with the financing and sustainability of capex growth in question (O'Dwyer, JPM credit).
Governor-imposed constraints on new data center builds could affect 37.5 GW of the 96 GW expected in 2028, with another 15 GW subject to conditions.
Holiday-thinned liquidity, with HT volumes down 56% and activity at 3 or 4 out of 10 in EMEA.
A stronger dollar (DXY above 102) weighing on ex-AI stocks.
Higher bond yields and a Fed that is weighing more hikes.
Consumers show signs of strain even as they keep spending (CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor link).
vol_and_positioning: Creager: CTAs had flipped short, and net and momentum length hit lows, leaving fuel for the rally. The move looks driven by systematic, CTA, vol-tracking and futures buying and by hedges coming off.

Dubravko: Momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 76th percentile. Levered ETFs sold about $60bn on Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday, taking exposure below January 2026 levels. CTAs are net short and vol targeters' leverage fell from the 65th to the 30th percentile, with about $50bn left to sell. Dealer net gamma imbalance is at the 12th percentile.
QQQ RSI dipped below 30, which has on average been followed by about a 4% rally over the next five trading days (Dubravko).
Sinha expects volatility to stay elevated until AI momentum recovers, and suggests a year-end hedge given the DXY breakout.
The desk would consider US Memory and Semis plays via options (Monetization Menu).
geopolitical: Developments in the Middle East are listed by Dubravko as a catalyst. The market is seemingly shifting to the view that geopolitical escalation odds are lower (Creager).
EU envoys agreed new Russia sanctions listings on banks, the shadow fleet and misinformation (Reuters link).
Trump's plan to import Russian diesel has stalled on the high seas (WSJ link).
The US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027 (NBC link). APEC Economic Leaders Meeting is Nov 18-19 in Shenzhen.
A US government funding deadline falls on Dec 11.
cross_bank_references: The note cites JPM's own Cembalest ('Eye on the Market') and Strouse on data center moratoriums, but no other banks.

tension_points.bull_case: The CRWV beat and raise eased funding concerns. Positioning is light (CTAs net short, momentum crowding reset, levered ETF exposure below January levels), and Dubravko sees room for a year-end rally and QQQ RSI below 30 has led to about +4% over five days.
tension_points.bear_case: Heavey sees only a marginal inflection and expects NVDA to tread water. Bowman calls the move AI FOMO rather than a broad improvement. EMEA high-touch shows no dip buying and some selling into strength. AI momentum remains weak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hotter than expected PPI print on Nov 13 following the post-CPI yield surge, or another Semis decline.

tension_points.bull_case: Falling AI capex is unlikely to cause a recession because it did little to add jobs, and consumers hold large cash balances in a labor market near full employment.
tension_points.bear_case: The recession basket is +14.9% since Sep 30 and there are financing risks, a possible 2028 data center pause on 37.5 GW, and wealth effects for top-decile consumers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Data center moratoriums putting projects under construction at risk, which the desk does not expect for 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: The CRWV beat and raise solved funding concerns, and positioning leaves fuel for further upside in the AI trade.
theme_stances.evidence: more legs for further upside in the AI trade

theme_stances.key_argument: Above-trend growth and robust earnings leave the market on a bullish trajectory, and the yield reset matches growth.
Today's price action reflects renewed AI FOMO, not a decisive improvement in the broader market undercurrents.
